How to build a Cloudbuster ⬇️

I am copper-maxing in my garden this year. I’m sure it’s just a coincidence my garden boxes are going crazy! I couldn’t believe the amount of flowers on my blackberries this morning. That box has 3 copper electroculture rods. I’m sure just a coincidence.

I also decided to build a cloud buster. The “from this” to “to this” snippets are 20 minutes apart by the way…after I got water flowing through my buster. Another coincidence I’m sure.

Most people have never even heard of a Cloudbuster.

It’s a device that some believe can help restore balance to the atmosphere using upright metal pipes and water. Whether you see it as forgotten science…historical curiosity…or simply an interesting DIY project, it’s one of those old ideas that has fascinated people for decades 👀

If you’d like to build one, start with five or six conductive metal pipes cut to the same length. I just brought 5 feet copper pipes at Home Depot.

Keep the tops of the pipes open and secure them in a hole 1-2 feet deep and 1-2 feet wide. You don’t want the pipes touching. Set the lower ends into the ground and surround with gravel like I did here. This creates a basin where you can pour water into or do a drip. Water is a crucial part of the busted…

Some people simply refill the water as needed, while others keep a slow, continuous flow of water running through the reservoir with a hose or small pump.

It is believed the metal tubes pull the energy from the sky and the water carries it away.

Place the finished Cloudbuster in an open area with a clear view of the sky, away from large buildings and trees.

There isn’t one universally accepted design, so you’ll find different pipe materials, spacing, and base layouts depending on who’s building it. Just build and OBSERVE.

Backyard science projects they should be doing in school.

This is the version I built on my homestead.

Whether you believe it works or you’re simply curious about unusual ideas from the past, it’s a fascinating project to research and build…and see all of the crazy coincidences, ya know? 😂

📡 Fifteen countries call for prohibition of any attack or threat against nuclear facilities

📌 London, IRNA – Fifteen countries, including Iran, China and Russia, have stressed that peaceful, safeguarded nuclear facilities must never be subjected to any attack or threat of attack.

In a joint statement on Thursday issued during the 70th General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), 15 countries underlined the need for clear and firm opposition to any attack or threat against nuclear facilities, urging all IAEA members to stand united in protecting peaceful nuclear activities and preserving the credibility of the Agency’s safeguards system.
​
The statement was released by Belarus, Brazil, Burkina Faso, China, Cuba, Indonesia, the Islamic Republic of Iran, Iraq, Nicaragua, Niger, Pakistan, Russia, South Africa, Tajikistan and Zimbabwe.
​
The countries warned that remaining silent in the face of attacks on safeguarded nuclear facilities undermines established international norms, weakens international legal order and prepares the ground to normalize such [destructive] moves.
